new: The headset menu is sharp too: like the story panel, the headset draws it itself, at the display's resolution.
Sharp text stays on in AR. A real hand in front of the panel or the menu does not hide it.
Sharp text is on by default in Quest Browser (layer, the cheapest). Rays, labels and notices still show over the panel and the menu.
Its row moved from the Debug tab to the menu's Settings tab, under My body.
test: Open the menu on a Quest in VR and AR: its text should be as sharp as the story panel's. Try every tab.
Point at the menu's buttons: the ray, its dot and the button's light show. Carry the menu with the grip and let it float.
The Story tab: the story's panels shown on the menu are drawn as before (not sharp), over the sharp menu.
Switch Sharp text to off on the menu's Settings tab and back: the menu should look as before, then sharp again.
Watch the frame rate with the menu open, with Sharp text on and off.
untested: The menu as a layer on a real headset: its place, its size, and how often it is written while you point at it.
The cost on a Quest at 90 Hz of a third layer and of writing the menu (5.5 MB each time it changes, up to twenty times a second while you point at it).
Other headsets and browsers: Sharp text is off there by default.
